operations.request: Analyze the CreateIssue API route in the supplied Gitea revision: identify its route registration, authentication and middleware controls, request decoding, and the complete path to the issue-creation effect.
operations.entryHint: Start with routers/api/v1/repo and routers/api/v1/api.go; follow relevant helpers and service calls within allowedPaths.

operations.request: Determine which authenticated principals can reach issue creation as repository readers and which repository, unit, or issue permissions the implementation actually requires; compare those effective controls with the supplied policy.
operations.entryHint: Trace repository and unit permission checks through models/perm, models/unit, models/repo, models/user, models/organization, and related route helpers.

operations.request: Trace authorization across the route-level controls, repository checks, issue-unit checks, issue-unit write checks, and any downstream issue-creation checks. Distinguish controls that are enforced from controls that are merely inferred or absent.
operations.entryHint: Follow calls from the API entry point through routers/api/v1/utils, services/context, services/issue, models/issues, and relevant permission models.

operations.request: Identify the issue creation effect and every authorization-relevant condition that must hold before it occurs, including repository state, enabled units, authentication, and any principal or resource-specific checks visible in the allowed source.
operations.entryHint: Follow the request data into the issue service/model effect and inspect conversion and settings code where it changes the authorization-relevant path.

operations.request: Identify relevant exceptions and alternate paths rather than treating endpoint-local checks as the whole authorization path, and state precise source or deployment limits that affect the conformance conclusion.
operations.entryHint: Check route registration, shared middleware, helper behavior, organization/repository distinctions, configuration and unit enablement, and any visible alternate entry points within allowedPaths.

questions.request: What is the complete source-trace from the CreateIssue API route entry to the issue creation effect, and where are authentication, repository, unit, and issue-specific controls applied?
questions.entryHint: Use the registered route and its called handlers/helpers, then continue into the issue creation service or model.

questions.request: Which authenticated repository readers and other principals can create an issue through this path under the implementation, and what exact checks determine that set?
questions.entryHint: Compare route middleware and permission predicates, including organization-owned or otherwise exceptional repository paths if present.

questions.request: Does the implementation conform to the independently supplied policy that any authenticated repository reader may create an issue when the issues unit is enabled, without requiring issue-unit write permission? Explain any overrestriction or underrestriction precisely.
questions.entryHint: Compare the effective source-derived authorization predicate with the policy; do not assume an endpoint-local check is the complete predicate.

premises.text: Any authenticated repository reader may create an issue when the issues unit is enabled. Issue-unit write permission is not required by this policy.

questions.request: Which controls are route-level, repository-level, issue-unit-level, or issue-resource-level, and does any downstream check add, remove, or change the effective authorization requirement before creation?
questions.entryHint: Name the relevant predicates and their call order, distinguishing enforcement from data validation or unrelated state checks.

questions.request: What exact preconditions and side effects govern creation of an issue, and which of them are authorization conditions versus repository or configuration conditions?
questions.entryHint: Inspect the final create operation and its inputs, including issue-unit enablement and repository state.

questions.request: What relevant exceptions, alternate route or middleware behavior, deployment configuration, or out-of-scope entry points could change the conformance result?
questions.entryHint: Report only exceptions supported by the allowed source or clearly identify them as source/deployment limits.

questions.request: Give a precise conformance conclusion for the supplied policy, including the effective principal/resource/operation predicate, relevant exceptions, and source or deployment limits.
questions.entryHint: Synthesize the traced route, shared controls, downstream effect, and policy comparison without expanding beyond the allowed source scope.
